We must assess each PP item. Scope individual. We need return exactly 53 objects. Need decide Violation/No Violation. Need be careful. Minimal criterion: syntactic, only role, means, optional ends. Operational decision: Violation when core story includes comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information that should be external. This is basically extra details beyond role-means-ends. But user story can include "so that". Need identify any implementation/testing/mockup notes etc. In these stories, many include specific details like "entering a name and optional description", "URL", "single multi-line text field", "by entering my name, email address, password and username", "up to 15 estimators", "two-minute countdown timer", "small thumbnail photo", "XHTML and CSS standards", "Internet Explorer 6 and 7 Firefox 1.5..." etc. Need decide if those are "means" details or extra information. The criterion says nothing more than role, means, optional ends. Means can have object and details. But some specifics are implementation hints? Example synthetic: "by entering a title and selecting a blue template" UI detail = violation. So we need flag UI/design/implementation specific details as violation? Many user stories include specific UI elements ("single multi-line text field", "URL", "page", "name on page", "small thumbnail photo"). The definition of Minimal means only role, means, optional ends. "Means" can be functional capability; extra specific technical constraints like database indexes, browser compatibility, standards compliance, Unicode, URLs, HTML/CSV export maybe functionalities? Need discern.
